body.statement:
Within the fully Markovian class \(Mone\), the compatible causal set is exactly
\[
 \Theta=F([0,1])=[L,U].
\]
Every comparison with the Ejaz--Bareinboim procedure is restricted to the intersection of its Definition~3.2 \(\rho\)-Markovian anchor class with the domain satisfying the separately stated Section~5 assumptions~(I)--(III).  Finiteness of the listed source and target groundings does not by itself establish the required global bound on relational-parent multiset size.  If \(F\) is nonconstant and \(Mone\) is included in that intersection, nonidentification transfers to every comparator class containing this intersection.  A return value \(\mathsf{FAIL}\) from the complete procedure on that domain does not alter the equality \(\Theta=[L,U]\) for \(Mone\), but \([L,U]\) is not asserted to be sharp for a strict comparator superclass.  If \(F\) is constant, then \(L=U\) identifies the query over \(Mone\); this singleton conclusion transfers only when the comparator-compatible class equals \(Mone\), not merely when it contains \(Mone\).  The unsupported status of \(rstar\) alone does not imply \(\mathsf{FAIL}\).
body.justification: The theorem is the exactly certifiable univariate specialization; its structural kernel is unconditional, and its comparator consequences are explicitly confined to the published anchor/Section 5 intersection.
body.gap: The interval is sharp for the fully Markovian class. A strict comparator superclass may contain additional values, and fixed finite groundings do not establish the global Section 5 parent bound.
body.consumer: Experiment 6.1 can accompany its fitted N3 point with the certified fully Markovian range and the exact class qualification needed for comparison with the neural procedure.
body.proof_tex:
Under \(\texttt{ass:one-unsupported-row}\) and \(\texttt{ass:binary-free-row}\), the generalized unsupported-row objects specialize to
\[
 \mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}=\{rstar\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}
 =\{(1-q,q):0\leq q\leq1\}.
\]
After the structural Markovian conditions are separated, \(\texttt{def:model-class}\) and \(\texttt{def:finite-unsupported-model-class}\) still impose identical membership requirements in this specialization: the same finite schema and graph, the same source and target groundings, mutually independent exogenous noises, no exogenous relational parent, no non-relational exogenous parent shared by distinct ground endogenous variables, type-shared mechanisms, reproduction of \(Psrc\), and use of \(K\) at every positive-source-support key.  Hence
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}=Mone,
 \qquad Q_{\mathrm{fin}}=Q.
\]
Replaying \(\texttt{def:multivariate-target-polynomial}\) at the unique free row \(p_{rstar}=(1-q,q)\) is exactly the replay defining \(F\).  This is also the equality supplied by \(\texttt{lem:polynomial-reduction}\), so
\[
 \Phi\bigl((1-q,q)\bigr)=F(q),
 \qquad 0\leq q\leq1.
\]
The specialization of \(\texttt{thm:sharp-finite-unsupported-rows}\) therefore gives
\[
 \Theta=F([0,1])
 =\left[\min_{q\in[0,1]}F(q),\max_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)\right],
\]
and its reverse inclusion is witnessed by compatible finite-noise, type-shared RSCMs.

It remains to identify these extrema with \(L\) and \(U\).  If \(F\) is nonconstant and \(c\in(0,1)\) is an optimizer, then for sufficiently small \(h>0\) the two one-sided difference quotients have opposite weak signs.  Since a polynomial is differentiable,
\[
 F'(c)
 =\lim_{h\downarrow0}\frac{F(c+h)-F(c)}{h}
 =\lim_{h\downarrow0}\frac{F(c)-F(c-h)}{h}
 =0.
\]
Thus every optimizer is either \(0\), \(1\), or a feasible distinct real root of \(F'\), and hence lies in \(Ccrit\) by \(\texttt{def:critical-candidates}\).  Conversely \(Ccrit\subseteq[0,1]\) and \(0,1\in Ccrit\).  Therefore
\[
 \min_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)=\min_{c\in Ccrit}F(c)=L,
 \qquad
 \max_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)=\max_{c\in Ccrit}F(c)=U.
\]
If \(F\) is constant, every value in \(F(Ccrit)\) is the same, and the same equalities follow from \(0,1\in Ccrit\).  This proves \(\Theta=F([0,1])=[L,U]\) without any comparator-domain assumption.

We now prove only the conditional comparator conclusions stated in the theorem.  Let \(\mathcal E_{\rho}\) denote the Ejaz--Bareinboim Definition~3.2 anchor class for the fixed causal problem, and let \(\mathcal E_5\) be its intersection with the domain satisfying the separately stated Section~5 assumptions~(I)--(III).  By the corrected \(\texttt{lem:ejaz-bareinboim-rho-markovian-scope}\), Definition~3.2 forbids exogenous relational parents but permits a non-relational exogenous parent to be shared only among attributes of the same instance.  The two structural restrictions recorded in \(\texttt{ass:no-exogenous-relational-parents}\) and \(\texttt{ass:no-shared-nonrelational-exogenous-parent}\) put every \(Mone\) model inside the Definition~3.2 anchor whenever the remaining anchor requirements are matched.  Section~5 has additional domain conditions.  In particular, its global relational-parent multiset bound is not implied by the fact that the finitely many listed source and target groundings have finite maximum degree.  Thus no inclusion \(Mone\subseteq\mathcal E_5\) is used unless it is supplied explicitly for the admissible skeleton family.

Assume now the inclusion required by the theorem's comparator clause, namely \(Mone\subseteq\mathcal E_5\), and suppose that \(F\) is nonconstant.  Then there exist \(q_1,q_2\in[0,1]\) such that \(F(q_1)\neq F(q_2)\).  Structural sharpness supplies \(M_1,M_2\in Mone\) with
\[
 Q(M_1)=F(q_1)\neq F(q_2)=Q(M_2).
\]
The inclusion gives \(M_1,M_2\in\mathcal E_5\), and the same two witnesses lie in every comparator class containing \(\mathcal E_5\).  Hence the query is not point identified in each such class.  This proves upward transfer only under the stated inclusion/intersection hypothesis.  Corollary~D.7 may be invoked to interpret the neural procedure's result only on \(\mathcal E_5\).  Whether that procedure returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\) or not, the structural argument already proved that \([L,U]\) is sharp for \(Mone\).  If a comparator class strictly contains \(Mone\), the inclusion supplies no upper or lower restriction on the additional models, so it cannot prove that \([L,U]\) is sharp there.

If \(F\) is constant, the structural part gives \(L=U\) on \(Mone\).  Equality of the comparator-compatible class with \(Mone\) transfers this singleton immediately.  Mere strict containment does not: constancy of a function on a subset says nothing about its values on new elements.  This proves the constant-case qualification.

Finally, unsupportedness alone does not force \(\mathsf{FAIL}\).  Consider an acyclic two-node target with a supported fair binary node \(A\), an unsupported binary node \(X\) with success probability \(q\), independent noises, no exogenous relational parents, no shared non-relational exogenous parent, and event \(B=\{A=X\}\).  Direct factorization gives
\[
 P(B\mid\operatorname{do}(a))
 =(1-q)\frac12+q\frac12=\frac12.
\]
The unsupported row is target relevant but cancels, so the causal query is point identified in this instance.  Type sharing is load bearing for the asserted one-parameter image: with two independent target nodes using the same unsupported binary key and the event of exactly one success, the shared-row map is
\[
 2q(1-q)\leq\frac12.
\]
If type sharing is removed while the other conditions are retained, occurrence-specific rows \(q_1=1\) and \(q_2=0\) make that event have probability one.  These finite examples verify both the cancellation claim and the necessity of the common coordinate \(q\).
